title: Day 596 — Mexico Peace Index: Biggest Gains in a Decade; 2,377 km Rail Mega-Plan; Sheinbaum Dismisses Trump Intervention Threat
detail: On May 20, 2026 (Day 596, Wednesday), President Claudia Sheinbaum's morning mañanera covered three major topics. MEXICO PEACE INDEX 2026: The Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP) released the Mexico Peace Index 2026, which recorded a 5.1% improvement in peace in 2025 — the most significant single-year improvement in at least a decade and the sixth consecutive year of progress. Total homicides fell 22.7% (approximately 7,000 fewer deaths than 2024), the largest single-year absolute decline on record. Sheinbaum highlighted the data as validation of her security strategy. The IEP report also noted ongoing structural risks: rising disappearances, extortion, and domestic violence indicate that the improvement in lethal violence has not uniformly translated into greater community safety. RAIL INFRASTRUCTURE MEGA-PLAN: Sheinbaum announced ambitious federal plans to construct 2,377 km of new passenger and cargo railway lines, including the Mexico City–Pachuca, Mexico City–Querétaro, Querétaro–Irapuato, and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo corridors, as well as a Tren Maya cargo extension. The plan also includes major road and water works across 2,300 municipalities. The announcement positions rail infrastructure as a cornerstone of the administration's economic and nearshoring diversification agenda ahead of the USMCA review. TRUMP INTERVENTION DISMISSAL: Sheinbaum addressed reports of U.S. figures seeking to 'intervene' in Mexico, drawing a distinction between statements from some individuals close to Donald Trump and Trump himself, whose position she characterized as more measured. She reiterated the sovereignty principle: Mexico will engage in cooperation but not subordination with any foreign government. NEW SCHOOL DEFENSE (NEM): Sheinbaum defended the Nueva Escuela Mexicana curriculum at the mañanera, stating its goal is to form critical and civic citizens, not rote memorization, and accusing prior administrations of having removed historical figures and national facts from textbooks.

media.caption: IEP Mexico Peace Index 2026: 5.1% peace improvement, 22.7% homicide decline in 2025 — most significant annual gains in at least a decade

title: Day 596 — Sheinbaum Signs 'Precio Justo' White Corn Agreement; García Harfuch: Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya Loses Federal Guard Protection
detail: On May 20, 2026 (Day 596), two additional significant developments emerged from the presidential agenda. PRECIO JUSTO WHITE CORN AGREEMENT: At 11:00 hrs, President Sheinbaum signed the national 'Precio Justo' (Fair Price) agreement creating a System for Ordering the Production and Commercialization of White Corn. The voluntary agreement covers 61,000 corn producers, 705,000 hectares of cultivated land, and 7 million tons of white corn production annually. It involves participation from major corn flour mills covering 80% of formal sector commercialization — including Maseca/Gruma and other large millers. The pact's dual goal: guarantee fair prices to producers and stabilize consumer prices in an environment where international corn prices had risen up to 50% due to supply chain disruptions and dollar-denominated commodity markets. Input (fertilizer and seed) discounts of 13–60% were negotiated as part of the accord. Sheinbaum signed the agreement amid ongoing protests by agricultural transporters (campesinos and transportistas) demanding better price guarantees and security against highway extortion. ROCHA MOYA FEDERAL PROTECTION ENDS: Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch clarified at the mañanera that suspended Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya — who is on 30-day leave following his April 29 U.S. DOJ indictment for alleged Los Chapitos ties — is still in Sinaloa but is no longer receiving Guardia Nacional protection. His security is now handled entirely by state police. The announcement reflects the federal government's calibrated management of the politically sensitive case, providing state-level protection while avoiding the optics of federal forces guarding an indicted official. Rocha Moya has neither surrendered to U.S. authorities nor been detained in Mexico, where FGR found insufficient grounds for extradition detention.

media.caption: Sheinbaum signs 'Precio Justo' white corn agreement covering 61,000 producers, 705,000 hectares and 7M tons amid agricultural producer protests
